n: Nephi warns his own people not to feel superior to the Gentiles. Being of Israel’s lineage saves no one; only keeping the commandments does.
Any Gentile who repents becomes part of God’s covenant people, while unrepentant Israelites are cut off. Covenant belonging depends on faith in Christ, not ancestry.

f.g: Here explicitly identified with God’s Son, Jesus Christ.

n: After the book comes forth and is sealed up again, many Gentiles will believe it and take it to Lehi’s descendants.

f.w: carry them forth unto the remnant of our seed

n: Through it, Lehi’s descendants will learn their origin: that their ancestors left Jerusalem and that they are of Israelite descent.

f.g: Here meaning people from the kingdom of Judah; Lehi was of Joseph’s tribe through Manasseh (Alma 10:3).

n: They will be taught the gospel of Jesus Christ and regain the knowledge of Christ their forefathers once had.
They will rejoice to see this as God’s blessing. Spiritual “scales of darkness” will fall from their eyes, and they will become a pure and delightsome people.

f.g: Delightful, pleasing—here to God, in faithfulness.

n: Scattered Jews will also begin to believe in Christ and gather, and believers will likewise become delightsome to God.

f.w: gather in upon the face of the land

n: God will begin a worldwide work among every nation, people, and language to restore his people.
Nephi now quotes Isaiah 11: the Lord will judge the poor fairly and defend the meek. His word alone—“the rod of his mouth”—will defeat the wicked.
Nephi inserts his own explanation into Isaiah’s words: a great division is coming. The Lord will spare the righteous even if the wicked must be destroyed by fire.
Righteousness and faithfulness will be like a belt the Messiah wears—his defining qualities, always with him.

f.g: Reins = kidneys or inner self; the girdle is a belt. Faithfulness binds him through and through.

n: Predators and prey will live together in peace, led by a little child—a picture of the peaceful Millennium.

f.w: the wolf dwell with the lamb

f.g: A young animal fattened for food.

n: Even the cow and bear will graze together, and the lion will eat straw—violence removed from creation itself.

f.w: the lion shall eat straw like the ox

n: An infant could play by a snake’s hole without harm. Enmity between humans and serpents, begun in Eden, will end.

f.g: A legendary deadly serpent; here a poisonous viper.

n: Nothing will hurt or destroy, because the earth will be as full of the knowledge of God as the ocean is full of water.

f.w: as the waters cover the sea

f.g: God’s temple-mount and, by extension, his kingdom.

n: Leaving Isaiah, Nephi adds that in that day the history and secrets of all nations will be made known.

f.w: all things shall be made known

n: Every secret will come to light and every sealed thing will be opened, including the sealed portion of the book.
Everything God has revealed will be revealed again, and Satan will lose his power over hearts for a long time—the thousand years of peace. Nephi ends this sermon.

f.w: Satan shall have power over the hearts of the children of men no more
